scenes.name: Doom, super-doom y stoner rock
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: El doom (exageración lenta, gótica y barroca de los grooves de Black Sabbath) crece en Inglaterra: Paradise Lost, Cathedral (las largas suites líricas de Forest Of Equilibrium), My Dying Bride y Electric Wizard, que infla la pesadez hasta que la música ya no fluye, solo retumba (Come My Fanatics, Dopethrone); Orange Goblin, Katatonia. El «super-doom» de los Melvins sigue en Seattle con Earth (drones colosales entre La Monte Young y monstruos extraterrestres), Karp, Sunn, y el «sludgecore» del Sur (Eyehategod, Harvey Milk). El stoner rock: Kyuss, Queens Of The Stone Age, Sleep, Fu Manchu, Monster Magnet, Wellwater Conspiracy, Boris.

xref.title: Band Name Origin (1963)
xref.body: While rehearsing in Birmingham, England, across from a cinema playing a 1963 horror movie titled "Black Sabbath," bassist Geezer Butler observed people paying good money to be scared. This sparked the idea for the band to create music that would also scare and shock people, leading them to rename themselves from "Earth" to "Black Sabbath" after the movie. "One day they noticed that the cinema was playing a 1963 horror movie entitled Black Sabbath."

xref.title: Suicidal Ideation and Depression (1993-1994)
xref.body: Following an overdose in July 1993, Kurt Cobain confessed in an interview with the British magazine The Face that he had "always been suicidal." His depression deepened in the fall of 1993, when he was frequently described as "strung out" and "semi-conscious." On legal documents related to a new book about Nirvana, he even listed his address as "hell on earth," underscoring his profound mental distress. "In the days after, he gave an interview to the British magazine The Face, where he convinced I've always been suicidal."

xref.title: Ghost (Sweden, 1996) – Papa Emeritus = Tobias Forge; Nameless Ghouls; Arena-Level Success Despite Satanic Imagery
xref.body: Ghost came together in Sweden in 1996 and became a worldwide phenomenon filling arenas. The only named member is the frontman Papa Emeritus (stage name of Tobias Forge), who dresses like a Pope from hell and cycles through different character names (Cardinal Copia, Papa Emeritus IV). All other band members are called Nameless Ghouls, each representing an ancient element (fire, water, wind, earth, plus ether). Rumored past Ghouls have included Dave Grohl. The satanic imagery has caused problems in the US Bible Belt. Their sound is a blend of hard metal, arena rock, doom metal, psych, symphonic metal, and gothic rock. "Ghost is hard metal, metal, arena rock, do metal, psych, symphonic metal, gothic rock, and more."

xref.title: Edwin Left 1997 Solo; Brian Byrne Tape Initially Thrown Out, Then Hired; Edwin Returned 2016
xref.body: I Mother Earth formed when Jagori Tanna and Christian Tanna met Edwin at their shared rehearsal space in 1990, creating a band immediately subject to a major-label bidding war. Edwin left in 1997 to go solo, finishing tour commitments that summer. The following year, auditions began; hundreds of demo tapes arrived, including one from a Newfoundlander named Brian Byrne that was immediately discarded. A mutual friend insisted they look again; Brian got a second chance, got the gig, and served as singer from 1998 to 2003. After a long hiatus, a 2012 reunion brought Brian back; Edwin was invited back again in 2016. Both occasionally share the stage on current tours. "His tape was immediately thrown out."

xref.title: First Zero-G Music Video (2014)
xref.body: OK Go partnered with Russian airline S7 to produce the first-ever Zero-G music video for their song "Upside Down and Inside Out." The video was filmed by flying a plane through a series of extreme parabolic trajectories, creating momentary periods of zero gravity. While Commander Chris Hadfield filmed a Zero-G video in space in 2013, OK Go's video is recognized for being filmed within the Earth's atmosphere. "Ok go teamed with a Russian airline called S7 to create the first ever Zero-G Music video for a song called Upside Down and Inside Out."

xref.title: Major Label Signing by Rob Cavallo
xref.body: Producer Rob Cavallo convinced Green Day to sign with a major label, a decision that went against the core ethos of the punk culture they emerged from. This controversial move led to the band being banned from some of their usual venues and labeled as "sell-outs" by many Bay Area punks. "He convinced Green Day that the only way forward was for them to sign with a major label. So going against the ethos of the punk culture they had grown up in, Green Day signed. That was a huge risk. And it got them banned from some of the places they used to play. As far as a lot of Bay Area punks were concerned, Green Day was dead to them. There were sell-outs."

xref.title: Post-Retirement Wealth – Joey's Day Trading; Johnny's Baseball Cards and Movie Posters Sold for $250,000+
xref.body: The Ramones never sold many records during their career — only one album (a greatest hits collection) went gold. Most income came from touring and merchandise. However, after the band retired in 1996, both Joey and Johnny found financial success outside music. Joey discovered stock market day trading in the late 1990s, taking tips from financial TV channels and reportedly amassing a substantial fortune before his death in 2001. Johnny, a lifelong Yankees fanatic who ranked baseball above rock and roll on his personal top-ten lists, spent decades collecting vintage baseball cards and movie posters, including original posters from *Frankenstein* (1931) and *The Day the Earth Stood Still* (1951). Per his will, the poster collection was sold at auction in Dallas after his death in 2004, netting more than a quarter of a million dollars for his wife Linda. "Two of whom — Joey and Johnny — made a lot of money after the band retired on things other than music."

xref.title: Producer of Green Day's Dookie
xref.body: Rob Cavallo produced Green Day's album *Dookie*. He was instrumental in convincing the band to sign with a major label, offering them $300,000 without having ever seen them perform live, and had previously worked with The Goo Goo Dolls, while his father managed Love & Spoonful and Earth, Wind & Fire. "He convinced Green Day that the only way forward was for them to sign with a major label. He'd signed the Goo Goo dolls and his dad had once managed the love and spoonful and earth-winded fire. And after hearing some Green Day, he offered them $300,000. And that was without ever seeing them play live."

xref.title: The Thin White Duke Persona - Thomas Jerome Newton Influence
xref.body: This amoral, hollow, damaged, and emotionless character, with his signature white shirt and waistcoat, emerged from an autobiography Bowie began while filming "The Man Who Fell to Earth," in which he played the doomed space alien Thomas Jerome Newton. Bowie loved the character and asked to keep the costuming, directly influencing his look for the next couple of years. "This character came from a sort of autobiography Bowie had begun while filming the man who fell to Earth, the movie where he played a doomed space alien named Thomas Jerome Newton."

xref.title: Vocals on Earth's "Divine and Bright" (Pre-Nevermind)
xref.body: Before Nirvana's "Nevermind" album was released, Kurt Cobain contributed guest vocals to the song "Divine and Bright" by the band Earth, as a favor to his friend Dylan Carlson. The recording of this song was unavailable for many years due to Carlson's struggles with addiction but was eventually reissued in 2010 on Earth's album, "A Bureaucratic Desire for Extra Capsular Extraction." "As a favor to Dylan, a pre-never-mind Kurt offered up some vocals on a song called Divine and Bright that disappeared for years because Dylan was an addict and couldn't hold it together. In 2010, a collection of recordings from that time was reissued on an album called A Bureaucratic Desire for Extra Capsular Extraction, and Divine and Bright is included."

xref.title: YouTube Breakout with One Guitar Cover
xref.body: Walk Off The Earth achieved their "big break" after posting a YouTube video featuring five members playing a single guitar to cover Gotye's "Somebody That I Used To Know." This video garnered 21 million views, propelling them to online fame. "Walk The Earth and their big break after they posted a YouTube video of five members playing this song on guitar? 21 million views later."

xref.title: Ziggy Stardust - Breakthrough and Theatricality
xref.body: The creation of Ziggy Stardust brought Bowie out of almost a decade of obscurity, elevating rock's theatricality to new levels. The character was presented as a "doomed spaceman with a Messiah concept," potentially involved in populating Earth with "Japanese style kabuki actors." Bowie used Ziggy to explore fashion, utilize his professional mime training from the 1960s, and experiment with art and sexuality. "this was the move that brought Bowie out of obscurity after almost a decade of dead ends."
